reasons: The principle of subdividing the existing dwelling into two self-contained one-bed flats is considered acceptable. The site lies within an established residential area of Balby in the Doncaster Main Urban Area, the proposed use is residential in a residential area, and the proposal makes effective use of an existing building, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 1 and 10 and NPPF paragraph 124. The sequential test and flood matters under Policy 57 are dealt with under flood risk below and do not undermine the principle.

The flood risk and drainage position is considered acceptable subject to conditions. The site is in Flood Zone 2, but the proposal is a change of use with a small extension, which NPPF paragraph 176 exempts from the sequential and exception tests. The submitted Flood Risk Assessment does not yet confirm the flood zone, fluvial flood levels, safe access and escape for the ground-floor flat, or a coherent drainage strategy, and the application form is inconsistent on surface water disposal. These shortcomings can be resolved through a revised assessment, drainage details, resilience measures and a flood warning and evacuation plan, so the development can be made safe for its lifetime without increasing flood risk elsewhere, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 56 and 57 and NPPF paragraphs 170, 175, 176, 181 and 182.

The effect on residential amenity is considered acceptable subject to conditions. Both flats are self-contained and exceed the minimum floor area for a one-bed, one-person unit, and the ground-floor flat has a rear courtyard and two stores. Dimensioned details of the first-floor rear extension, glazing details for the new rear window, sound insulation between the flats, storage and courtyard allocation, and a one-person occupancy limit for each flat will ensure no unacceptable harm to the daylight, outlook or privacy of the neighbouring occupiers at Nos. 15 and 19, and adequate living conditions for future occupiers, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10, 44 and 45 and NPPF paragraph 135.

The design and effect on the character of the area is considered acceptable subject to conditions. The front elevation of the mid-terrace house is unchanged, and the first-floor extension is at the rear, flat-roofed, below the main eaves and shown in brick to match the existing dwelling. Control over facing materials and roof covering will ensure the extension integrates with the host property and the terrace, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 41 and 44 and NPPF paragraphs 135 and 139.

The highways and parking impact is considered acceptable. The proposal adds a single household to a residential close, with no new access, and would not be expected to cause an unacceptable highway safety impact or a severe cumulative impact on the road network. Secure cycle storage and refuse and recycling arrangements can be secured by condition, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13 and NPPF paragraphs 115 and 116.
conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: Required by Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans and documents listed on the decision notice. Reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the application as approved.

Before the flats are first occupied, a revised site-specific flood risk assessment confirming the Flood Zone 2 designation, the fluvial flood level (including a climate change allowance) and safe access and escape arrangements shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. The flood resilience measures set out in the Flood Risk Assessment (including raised door thresholds, flood-resilient ground-floor finishes and raised electrical services) shall be implemented before either flat is first occupied and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure the development is safe for its lifetime, reduces the consequences of flooding to occupiers and property, and does not increase flood risk elsewhere, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 57 and NPPF paragraphs 170 and 181.

Prior to commencement of the development, details of foul and surface water drainage, including the surface water discharge point, sustainable drainage measures, and confirmation that run-off will not exceed existing rates, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure satisfactory drainage and no increase in flood risk on or off the site, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 56 and NPPF paragraph 182.

Prior to first occupation of the flats, a flood warning and evacuation plan, including signing up to the Environment Agency flood warning service, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and made available to occupiers. Reason: To ensure any residual flood risk can be safely managed, in accordance with NPPF paragraph 181.

Before the first-floor rear extension is commenced, dimensioned plans and elevations of the extension (depth, height, eaves and ridge levels, and distances to the boundaries with Nos. 15 and 19) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To protect the daylight, outlook and living conditions of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 44.

The new first-floor rear window shall be glazed in accordance with a glazing specification approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the extension is brought into use, and shall be retained as approved. Reason: To protect the privacy of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 44.

The external walls of the first-floor rear extension shall be constructed in facing materials (brick or render) that match the existing dwelling in colour, coursing, bond and texture, in accordance with samples or details submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the extension is built above damp-proof course level. Reason: To ensure the extension integrates visually with the host property and the terrace in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 41 and 44.

The roof covering and any rainwater goods to the rear extension shall be installed in accordance with details submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before installation. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance and secure the quality of the approved design in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 44.

Before the flats are first occupied, a scheme of sound insulation between the ground-floor and first-floor flats, to a standard agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority, shall be installed and retained. Reason: To secure an acceptable level of residential amenity for future occupiers in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10 and 44.

Before the flats are first occupied, details of the internal storage for each flat, the allocation of the rear courtyard between the two flats, and secure, covered cycle storage for each flat shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and implemented and retained as approved. Reason: To ensure adequate storage and amenity space for future occupiers and to promote sustainable travel in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 13 and 44.

Prior to occupation, details of refuse and recycling storage and the arrangements for presenting bins for collection shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the approved arrangements shall be implemented and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure that waste storage and collection does not obstruct the highway or footway and to protect highway safety, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13.

Each flat shall be occupied by no more than one person. Reason: The flats have been assessed as one-bed, one-person units against the minimum space standard, and occupation by more people would not provide sufficient internal space under Doncaster Local Plan Policy 45.
